title: The Tragedy of the Commons and Open-Source Burnout
explainer: Ecologist Garrett Hardin's 1968 essay in Science described how a shared resource that costs individual users nothing to draw on, but costs someone real effort to maintain, tends toward overuse and neglect unless that maintenance cost is absorbed by someone. A widely-depended-on open-source project is a modern instance of exactly this dynamic: thousands of downstream users draw on code maintained, often unpaid, by one or two people — the economic root of maintainer burnout and the 'bus factor' risk that upstream contributors have to manage.
